title: The minimum-norm interpolator
html:
Let X be n×p with rank r and singular values d1≥⋯≥dr>0, and let 𝛃β^+=X+y.

  1. (Characterization.) The least squares estimates are the vectors 𝛃β^++v with v∈N(X). Among them 𝛃β^+ is the only one in C(X⊤), and it has the smallest Euclidean norm. If r=n, then 𝛃β^+=X⊤(XX⊤)−1y and every least squares estimate interpolates: 𝛃Xβ^+=y.

  2. (Ridgeless limit.) For λ>0 let 𝛃β^λ=(X⊤X+λI)−1X⊤y be the ridge estimate. Then 𝛃𝛃𝛃‖β^λ−β^+‖≤(λ/dr2)‖β^+‖, so 𝛃𝛃β^λ→β^+ as λ↓0.

  3. (Gradient descent.) Let b0∈Rp, 0<η<2/d12 and bt+1=bt+ηX⊤(y−Xbt). Then 𝛃bt→β^++(I−P)b0. In particular, gradient descent started at b0=0 converges to 𝛃β^+.

  4. (Bias and variance.) If 𝛃E(Y)=Xβ and Cov(Y)=σ2I, then 𝛃E(X+Y)=Pβ and Cov(X+Y)=σ2∑i≤rdi−2vivi⊤. For every a∈Rp, 𝛃𝛃E(a⊤X+Y−a⊤β)2=(a⊤(I−P)β)2+σ2∑i=1r(a⊤vi)2di2,{#eq-hd-min-norm-mse}

    and 𝛃𝛃E‖X+Y−β‖2=‖(I−P)β‖2+σ2∑i≤rdi−2.
